messages:
alex_m: Seeing a sudden spike in 5xx from hosted API after the staged rollout to the canary slice. Customers reported timeouts. Gateway 502/504 went from ~0.2% -> ~12% in ~5m. Starting triage.

opsbot: ALERT: canary-slice(42) error_rate > 10% (5m avg) for route /v1/generate. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/err/42

samira: Noted. Correlating with a config flip at 09:08 UTC — we pushed header-normalizer and a route-weight increase. Diff: `feature.route_header_trim: false -> true`, weight 5% -> 30%.

julie_p: Header trim was experimental. If it chops long Authorization headers (long JWTs) upstream auth likely rejects -> gateway surfaces 502/504. We saw similar in staging but lower token sizes.

oncall-sre: Pulling gateway logs now. Sample from proxy: ```
2026-03-17T09:09:12.123Z gateway[proxy-42] ERROR auth/proxy.go:178 upstream auth returned 502 for request id=aa1b2c client=svc-frontend token_len=9234
2026-03-17T09:09:12.124Z gateway[proxy-42] WARN route/router.go:91 transformed headers: Authorization truncated to 8192
```

alex_m: Can we rollback the canary config quickly? I can run `redwoodctl` if someone gives thumbs. Need minimal blast radius.

samira: I can rollback. Plan: 1) set canary weight -> 0% 2) rollback to rev `rev-20260317-0812` (pre-change) 3) confirm healthchecks. Command I'll run: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --slice=canary --to=rev-20260317-0812`

julie_p: Recommend step ordering: scale weight to 0% first (avoid mixing kernels/headers) then rollback. Also disable `route_header_trim` in flight. I'll watch metrics and auth logs.

opsbot: ACTION: rollback initiated by samira at 09:14 UTC. Job id: rb-1749997771-1

samira: Done. Canary weight -> 0%. Rollback complete. Containers back to rev-20260317-0812. Healthchecks passing on all canary backends. 5xx dropping: now 0.6% (5m avg).

alex_m: Confirmed customers we had repro from (cust-A) re-tested, errors cleared. Good.

julie_p: Follow-up items: add a regression test to devex for header lengths >8k, add lint preventing header_trim toggle without a canary abort rule, and add an automated canary hold if 5xx > 2% for 2m. I'll open PRs.

oncall-sre: Logging a follow-up incident ticket and creating a short runbook update for header-related canary flags. Please attach any customer repros.

alex_m: I'll file the postmortem and include repro steps and timeline. Also flag billing ops in case any customers got rate-limited/invoiced incorrectly during the window.

samira: quick repro note to include: send a request with Authorization header ~9KB, canary with header_trim=true returns 502; with header_trim=false returns 200. Curl snippet: ```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $(python -c 'print("x"*9200)')" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

julie_p: Thanks — pushing the canary gating rules now. Moving to post-incident actions. :white_check_mark:
